text:
Zoe (Release Lead): heads-up: DeployBot just auto-reverted the EU canary after embedding error_rate crossed the threshold. Did we push a tokenizer config with that build?

DeployBot: autorevert: triggered by metric `error_rate_embeddings_eu` > 1.5% for 3m. Action: rolled canary back to model open-embed-2.3.1 at 2024-06-12T11:22Z. Autorevert reason: tokenization_exceptions rising. Autorevert policy: enabled.

Harish (Runtime): I see PR #8599 touched tokenizer_v2 -> changed pre-token normalization. That would explain the exception spike. The model binary expected legacy-normalization.

Mei (SRE): rollback completed, pods healthy. However traffic router still shows a leftover 5% pinned to the new variant in eu-canary slice. Manual routing cleanup needed.

Zoe (Release Lead): noted. Mei, can you flush the route pin to 0%? Also, should we un-suppress autorevert for future canaries or change thresholds?

Mei (SRE): doing route cleanup now: `curl -X POST https://router.internal/api/slices/eu-canary/actions -d '{"weight":0}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ROUTE_TOKEN'`

DeployBot: route update accepted. eu-canary weight -> 0%.

Mei (SRE): confirmed: routing at 0%, all traffic to stable. Monitoring `error_rate_embeddings_eu`, `p95_embed_latency_eu`, and `tokenizer_exceptions_eu`.

Harish (Runtime): repro steps in staging look consistent: toggling normalization off fixes exceptions. I have a quick patch to revert tokenizer config in the build pipeline (branch: tokenizer/legacy-normalize-fix). Will run staging verification.

Nora (DevEx): for release notes & changelog: short line: "Canary rollout temporarily reverted in EU for embedding model due to tokenizer compatibility issue; stable model serving restored." Tom, want a CS-friendly blurb?

Tom (CS): yes, short customer message: "We temporarily reverted an EU embedding model canary after we detected increased embedding errors. We've restored the prior model and are testing a safe fix. No customer data impacted. We'll follow up if we need to re-run the rollout." I'll post to incident page after Harish confirms staging pass.

Zoe (Release Lead): decision: keep release branch frozen for model changes until we verify pipeline will enforce tokenizer compatibility. Owners: Harish=fix+verify, Mei=monitor+routing, Nora=docs, Tom=customer comms.

Harish (Runtime): running staging verification now. steps: ```
1) checkout tokenizer/legacy-normalize-fix
2) build image: `make image MODEL=open-embed-2.3.2-fix`
3) deploy to staging embed-canary
4) run embed smoke tests + tokenizer exception monitor
```

OpsBot: note: autorevert settings for canaries are currently: threshold=1.5%, window=3m, action=full-rollback.

Zoe (Release Lead): let's be conservative: change threshold -> 2.0% and window -> 5m for embedding canaries only, and enable slack alert annotations for the deploy channel. Benji, can we queue that change? (Benji is out but OpsBot can take a ticket)

OpsBot: creating config update ticket TICKET-RELEASE-171812: update canary autorevert thresholds for embedding models. Assigned to infra-config.

Mei (SRE): staging verification results in ~6m: tokenization_exceptions gone, embedding error_rate < 0.2%. Harish's patch looks good.

Harish (Runtime): pushed `open-embed-2.3.2-fix` image to canary registry. If we want to re-run the canary, recommend a gradual rollout and manual-suppress autorevert for the first 10m while we watch tokenizer_exceptions metric.

Zoe (Release Lead): prefer to keep autorevert enabled. Plan: 1) patch merged, 2) staged canary verification 30m stable, 3) small EU canary at 5% for 10m, 4) if stable, ramp to 50% then 100%. No manual suppression.

Nora (DevEx): drafting changelog entry and internal note: "Model canary reverted in EU due to tokenizer mismatch; fix merged and staged; planned gradual re-rollout with autorevert enabled." Will post to `#releases` and attach to the ticket.

Tom (CS): prepped CS draft and holding until Zoe confirms green. Link to internal incident: https://internal.redwood/status/INC-20240612-embed-canary.

Zoe (Release Lead): outcome: autorevert did its job and prevented a broader regression. Action items: Harish merge + verify, Mei confirm routing cleaned, Ops update autorevert thresholds per ticket, Nora/Tom finalize comms, schedule postmortem if we see recurrence. Closing thread; will reopen if any regressions. Thanks all :white_check_mark:
